Neros plans $615M drone manufacturing expansion in US
The Pentagon issued a $450 million conditional loan to the startup to scale its small-UAS production, with Neros pledging $165 million in equity toward the project.
Share Copy link Email LinkedIn X/Twitter Facebook Print
The Department of Defense issued small drone maker Neros a conditional loan of up to $450 million through its Office of Strategic Capital to support the company’s expansion plans in the United States, the agency announced Monday.
The funds will help increase Neros’ manufacturing capacity to produce dual-use small unmanned aircraft systems and ground control systems, according to the agency’s press release. The capacity expansion will also enable the company to produce critical components such as motors, radios, flight electronics, sensors and batteries.
In addition to the Pentagon’s loan commitment, Neros pledged $165 million in equity toward the project, bringing the investment amount to $615 million, the drone manufacturer said in a separate press release.
The DOD funding puts Neros on the path to manufacture 1 million drones per year by 2028, co-founder and CEO Soren Monroe-Anderson said in a statement.
The DOD funds will help Neros comply with updated requirements under the National Defense Authorization Act for fiscal year 2026.
